subject: AI buildout
title: The AI buildout: who gets paid, and in what order
deck: Every new AI data center pays a chain of businesses, from chip designers to power companies. Each link has its own story.
body: When a cloud company adds AI capacity, its money moves in order: it buys processors, houses them in a data center, and connects the building to the power grid. Each step pays a different kind of business.

Alphabet, Google's parent, reported $51.4 billion of capital spending in the three months to September 30, 2026, mainly on servers, network equipment and data centers. NVIDIA reported $107.6 billion of Data Center sales in its quarter ended October 25, 2026.
Kim's reading is that chip designers tend to be paid when hardware ships and utilities month by month once a building is switched on, with networking suppliers and landlords in between.
The last step has the widest gap. Dominion Energy, Virginia's main utility, counts about 54 GW of data-center capacity under contract against a billed peak of 4.8 GW.
openQuestion: Which step in the chain turns AI spending into sales soonest, and which has the most still on paper?

connections.what: Design the processors that run AI work and sell them to the companies that fill data centers.
connections.basisLine: One company release cited. It gives NVIDIA's Data Center sales. It says nothing about the other three.
connections.known: NVIDIA reported Data Center sales of $107.6 billion for its quarter ended October 25, 2026.
connections.unknown: How much of each other chip company's sales comes from data centers.
connections.whereToLook: The segment tables in each company's quarterly report.

connections.what: Pay for the processors, servers and buildings, then rent the computing power to others.
connections.basisLine: One company filing cited. It shows Alphabet's spending. It does not name who Alphabet buys from, and it does not cover the other four companies.
connections.known: Alphabet reported $51.4 billion of capital spending for the three months ended September 30, 2026, mainly on technical infrastructure.
connections.unknown: Which cloud companies are growing fastest, and how each is paying for it.
connections.whereToLook: Each company's quarterly results: cloud sales, capital spending, debt and cash.

connections.what: Make the switches and cables that link thousands of processors into one system.
connections.basisLine: Kim's reading of how AI systems are built. No filing cited.
connections.unknown: How much cloud companies spend on networking for each dollar they spend on processors.
connections.whereToLook: Capital-spending breakdowns on cloud companies' earnings calls, and Broadcom's remarks on its AI networking sales.

connections.what: Own data-center buildings and rent space in them to companies that need room for their machines.
connections.unknown: Whether the large cloud companies rent from landlords or mostly build their own data centers.
connections.whereToLook: The customer and leasing sections of the landlords' annual reports, and the lease notes in each cloud company's filings.

connections.what: Supply the electricity that data centers run on.
connections.basisLine: One company presentation cited. It covers Dominion's own territory only.
connections.known: Dominion reported about 54 GW of data-center capacity under contract and a data-center billing peak of 4.8 GW as of August 2026.
connections.unknown: Which utilities have the most data-center demand under contract, and how fast it turns into sales.
connections.whereToLook: The utility's quarterly results and the load forecast it files with its grid operator.
